tenders.description_excerpt: Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at 14 Wing Greenwood (and its satellite sites in Nova Scotia) for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029). Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL. Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French). IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029. The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL. Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions

The FRSM will support NRC’s submarine hydrodynamics research for current and future submarine designs, enabling comprehensive testing in controlled and free-running environments. NRC encourages innovative solutions and does not prescribe a specific vehicle architecture. Offerors are expected to propose an integrated design that satisfies the operational, performance, and research objectives described in this Statement of Requirement. Background NRC’s Ocean, Coastal and River Engineering Research Centre (NRC-OCRE) conducts research in submarine hydrodynamics, vehicle dynamics, control systems, and operational safety using physical and numerical modelling techniques. Over the past two decades, NRC has developed and tested several scaled submarine models, including the “Albert” model, a free-running Victoria Class submarine research platform used to investigate hydrodynamic performance, handling characteristics, seakeeping behaviour, near-bottom operations, and related submarine operating scenarios. tenders.description_excerpt: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC), through its Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre (CEI) in Boucherville, Québec, is seeking information regarding commercially available large slurry mixers suitable for the preparation of viscous battery electrode slurries used in a battery prototyping line. The mixer will be used to prepare electrode slurries for advanced battery technologies, including lithium-ion and emerging battery chemistries. The equipment is intended to improve slurry preparation efficiency, process consistency, scalability, and operational flexibility while supporting research, development, and prototyping activities. The NRC requires a robust and versatile mixing platform capable of handling viscous slurries under controlled temperature and vacuum conditions while providing process monitoring and data logging capabilities. NRC is seeking information on equipment compatible with common battery slurry solvents, including water, N-Methylpyrrolidone (NMP), Gamma-Valerolactone (GVL), Dimethylformamide (DMF), and Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO). Lapping and polishing equipment are mission critical for a photonics foundry producing waveguides, modulators, lasers, filters, or integrated photonic circuits. These tools ensure substrate flatness, surface quality, and thickness uniformity, all of which directly affect optical performance, coupling efficiency, and device yield. The CPFC has a requirement to update its aging lapping and polishing tools degrade as they currently contribute to manufacturing risks to yield, optical performance, process stability, and throughput. Replacing aging tools is essential to maintain foundry grade capability, support customer programs, and prevent production interruptions as the CPFC progresses to 4” wafer processing capability. The CPFC provides advanced fabrication and metrology services for both internal research programs and external clients, enabling the development and production of cutting-edge photonic devices used in telecommunications, sensing, and quantum technologies. Photonic devices are critical pieces of hardware for high-performance computing in various innovative fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), data centres, automotive LiDARs (Light Detection and Ranging), biomedical, aerospace; security, and quantum industry/applications. The global market for compound semiconductor foundry services is growing rapidly, presenting niche opportunities and challenges for Canada. Limited access to compound semiconductor foundry services poses several challenges to develop, successfully introduce, and supply new products in an increasingly competitive marketplace. Photonic devices fabricated on InP wafers must undergo several “back-end” steps before dicing and packaging, adding time and cost if the assembled parts are then found to be defective. tenders.description_excerpt: The National Research Council Canada has a requirement for the supply of a 1.2 GHz acquisition bandwidth real-time spectrum analyzer (26.5 GHz) to capture and stream in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) data. The real-time spectrum analyzer will be used in a reverberation chamber to qualify DUTs against very stringent telescope protection levels. To achieve this, a low-noise, ultra-sensitive real-time spectrum analyzer is required. The real-time spectrum analyzer will capture and stream I/Q data that is used to reconstruct complex time domain signals that are then transformed to the frequency domain where radio astronomy techniques of spectral integration are used to reduce the standard deviation of the noise.

tenders.evaluation_summary: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the items detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Demolition Kit, Bangalore Tor...
tenders.description_excerpt: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the items detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2. The Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 is required as a specialized explosive charge used by combat engineers to breach barbed wire obstacles/entanglements and to clear a path through anti-personnel mines, without requiring personnel to approach the obstacle directly under fire. The system consists of several cylindrical sections of tubes/pipes that can be connected end-to end to create a linear explosive charge of desired length. A blunt, rounded nose sleeve is attached to the leading end of the assembly, allowing the torpedo to be pushed or shoved through obstacles, such as concertina wire or across rough terrain, without snagging. The Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 is primed with a blasting cap. When detonated, the pipe itself contributes to the effect: the metal casing fractures into high-velocity fragments that shred the surrounding wire, while the explosive blast clears a path for infantry to advance. The biological information obtained through sample processing supports annual stock assessments and the development of scientific advice regarding the status of BC herring stocks. The Contractor will be required to provide all qualified personnel, laboratory facilities, equipment, materials, and services necessary to process approximately 200 to 250 herring samples per year. Each sample typically contains approximately 100 fish, although sample sizes may vary. The Contractor must process all samples provided by DFO, including samples containing fewer than 100 fish, in accordance with DFO-approved scientific procedures. For each fish processed, the Contractor must record the fish's length, weight, sex, gonad length, gonad weight, maturity stage, and one suitable herring scale for subsequent age determination. All sample identification information and biological data must be entered into the MS Access database provided by DFO. The Contractor must also prepare herring scale slides, maintain daily electronic data backups, conduct quality control checks, and submit the required data and associated materials within the specified timelines. The project involves the replacement of approximately 110 m of deteriorated retaining wall and the reconstruction of the adjacent 2.0 m wide asphalt pathway located between Lake Annette and Ochre Lake within a high-use day-use area. Construction is anticipated to take place during Fall 2026 to reduce impacts on peak visitor use and take advantage of lower seasonal water levels. The existing natural stone retaining wall has experienced progressive deterioration, resulting in wall instability, pavement cracking, material loss, localized shoreline erosion, and reduced visitor safety. The objective of the project is to restore shoreline stability, improve visitor safety, and provide a durable, low-maintenance infrastructure solution that is compatible with the surrounding natural environment. tenders.description_excerpt: Canada’s coasts and oceans are an integral part of the country’s culture, identity, environment, and economy. The Small Craft Harbours (SCH) program of Fisheries and Oceans Canada is responsible for overseeing the administration and maintenance of a federally-owned system of fishing and recreational harbours in British Columbia, with the fishing harbour component delivered largely in partnership with local client-run Harbour Authorities. These harbours provide communities access to oceans, supporting commercial, recreational, and indigenous fisheries, marine recreation and tourism, aquaculture, and a variety of other uses that directly and indirectly contribute to Canada’s economy, supporting livelihoods in coastal communities and throughout the province. Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) requires accurate and up-to-date information describing the contributions of Small Craft Harbours (SCH) to British Columbia's coastal livelihoods and economy. tenders.description_excerpt: The purpose of this requirement is to obtain an independent actuarial costing analysis of the short-, medium- and long-term direct and indirect costs if the current federal workers’ compensation regime remains unchanged, or if two options for modernizing the regime are implemented. The analysis must include both overall costs of the regime, and costs for (a) the five federal employers with the highest volumes of workers’ compensation claims and (b) a selection of federal employers with moderate claim volumes. The analysis should also provide a return on investment (ROI) for the two modernization options.

tenders.description_excerpt: Title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors - 100032783 The Service Navigation Support for Seniors project will have two components. The first component, Component A will review the accessibility of information on support services available to seniors and/or their caregivers across all federal, provincial and territorial (FPT) jurisdictions and to identify common barriers. The objective of Component A is to understand what support services are the most frequently requested across the 14 FPT jurisdictions and why the access rate for information is more elevated, especially as it relates to barriers in accessing them. The second component, Component B, will use the results from Component A and identify, in collaboration with FPT Officials a number of case studies to analyse the mechanisms through which seniors and/or their caregivers learn about and/or access support services aiming to build awareness and improve access to service navigation supports. This would also include policy recommendations for jurisdictions to consider in enhancing service navigation support for seniors.

The near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz in early 2026 removed approximately 15 million barrels per day of global supply, making storage indicators one of the most important drivers of short-term crude oil pricing. At the same time, a significant disconnect remains between declining physical inventories and paper futures markets, increasing the need for accurate and timely inventory intelligence. Crude oil inventory and pipeline flow data are critical for supporting departmental analysis and briefings, as well as monitoring energy supply and security. To better understand North American oil markets and inform policy decisions, Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) requires greater visibility into Canadian crude oil inventories and pipeline flows. Specifically, the department requires weekly reports on crude oil inventory levels in Canada’s main storage areas, as well as daily and near-real-time pipeline flow data within Canada and for exports to the United States. tenders.description_excerpt: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) is Canada's largest independent administrative tribunal. It is responsible for making well-reasoned decisions on immigration and refugee matters, efficiently, fairly and in accordance with the law. The IRB decides, among other responsibilities, who needs refugee protection among the thousands of claimants who come to Canada annually. Every year, the Board renders thousands of decisions on refugee protection and immigration matters. At these hearings, refugees and immigrants who are not fluent in English or French count on the IRB to provide them with interpretive services. These interpretive services are required in a wide variety of languages and dialects, reflecting the diverse backgrounds of the refugees and immigrants who come to Canada. In order to manage the interpretive services required for such a large number of hearings, including urgent hearings, IRB issues contracts to interpreters who provide services on an “as-and-when-requested” basis and invoice for any services they provide. All interpreters are paid the same flat hourly rate. These contracts effectively work as a “roster” of potential interpreters who could be called upon to provide interpretive services at a hearing. tenders.description_excerpt: Industry Sustainment Business Case Analysis (SBCA) Workshops: NEW WORKSHOP DATE - TBD Purpose: The purpose of this notice is to invite industry representatives working in defence sustainment to participate in an upcoming online Industry Sustainment Business Case Analysis (SBCA) Workshop. An SA is a non-binding arrangement between Canada and a pre-qualified supplier that allows departments and agencies to award contracts and solicit bids from a pool of pre-qualified suppliers for specific requirements within the scope of the SA. An SA is not a contract for the provision of goods and services described in it and neither party is legally bound, as a result of signing a supply arrangement alone. The intent of a supply arrangement is to establish a framework to permit expeditious processing of individual bid solicitations, which result in legally binding contracts for the goods and services described in those bid solicitations.

tenders.description_excerpt: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) This bid solicitation cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 30004518 dated August 29, 2024 with a closing of October 16, 2025 at 14:00 Atlantic Time. Submissions for 30004518 will no longer be accepted. This solicitation will remain on CanadaBuys until June 30, 2029. The Canadian Hydrographic Service (CHS) of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has a requirement to establish a number of Supply Arrangement (SA) with pre-qualified suppliers to meet the general requirements specified in each of the following service streams: a. STREAM 1: Hydrographic/Bathymetric Training Services; b. STREAM 2: Hydrographic Navigational Charting Support and Production services; c. STREAM 3: Bathymetric Data Assessment and Processing services; and d. STREAM 4: Hydrographic/Bathymetric Consulting services. These services will be required on an as required basis throughout the period(s) of the Supply Arrangement. The Canadian Hydrographic Service (CHS) is mandated to chart Canadian waters to ensure safe navigation and to protect Canadian sovereignty. In that endeavour CHS must collect hydrographic/bathymetric data in support of new digital charting products as well as maintain existing portfolios of nautical charts in a variety of formats. This must be done using current international charting standards of data collection, processing and production.

tenders.description_excerpt: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) has launched a pilot project to compile a list of emerging, mid-career, and established professional Indigenous artists in the Atlantic Region. The list will be shared within federal departments and agencies in Atlantic Canada so that employees can use the list to procure Indigenous art for use in Government of Canada buildings and offices in New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. This opportunity is open to emerging, mid-career, or established Indigenous artists and artisans who create art or traditional crafts representative of the Indigenous Peoples in Atlantic Canada. To submit the required information for this opportunity complete the Indigenous Artist Form at the following link: https://forms-formulaires.alpha.canada.ca/en/id/cmc1xkjh8001ex601pjp4kwcj Once received, we will follow up to confirm if you are eligible. Please be advised that inclusion on the list is not a guarantee that your business will be contacted to provide services. For questions or comments, please contact mailto:pwgsc.basatlantic-scaatlantiquetpsgc@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca

To be eligible to participate: the principal place of business must be in Canada; your business must be owned by a member of an underrepresented group, which includes: women, visible minorities, persons with disabilities, and members of the 2SLGBTQQIA+ community (as per Annex A: Supplier Diversity Program Forms); and be able to provide catering services in at least one of the four provinces in the Atlantic Region (New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, Newfoundland and Labrador) To submit the required information for this opportunity complete the form at the following link: https://forms-formulaires.alpha.canada.ca/en/id/cmer94nwg012fyr01artk8l6c Once received, we will follow up to confirm if you are eligible. tenders.description_excerpt: The National Research Council on behalf of the Government of Canada (GoC) and its’ Partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction projects. This procurement includes the design, development, configuration, deployment and ongoing support of the platform. The solution will provide a centralized system that ensure consistent data collection, automated validation, and reporting in alignment with embodied carbon disclosure and reduction policies for buildings and infrastructure projects. At a minimum, the platform shall enable: - Intake of material and project specific embodied carbon submissions; - Import and export capabilities for compatible whole building Life Cycle Assessment (wbLCA) submission reports and raw data; - Dashboards and customizable reporting functions for internal analysis; and - The creation of an anonymized public dataset. The Platform MUST comply with Government of Canada security requirements for Protected A information and meet Canadian-based data residency requirements.

tenders.description_excerpt: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is providing advance notice of its intention to issue a new Invitation to Qualify (ITQ-D) in support of the Enterprise Data Hub initiative. PSPC has previously conducted procurement and industry engagement activities related to the Enterprise Data Hub, including previous Invitations to Qualify. PSPC now intends to launch a new ITQ-D through CanadaBuys. This Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) is being published for information purposes only to provide interested suppliers with advance awareness of the forthcoming procurement opportunity. No solicitation documents are being released through this notice, and suppliers are not required to respond at this time. The forthcoming ITQ-D will set out the applicable requirements, qualification process, evaluation criteria, and instructions for participation. Interested suppliers are encouraged to monitor CanadaBuys for the release of the ITQ-D and any related procurement notices. For additional background on the Enterprise Data Hub initiative and industry engagement activities conducted to date, interested suppliers may also review the previously published Summary of Feedback and Outcomes Report.

It is intended to result in the award of 5 (five) contracts for 5 (five) years. The Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS) offers free financial counselling and mediation services to farmers who are having difficulties meeting their financial obligations. It is a voluntary, private and confidential service that brings farmers and their creditors together with a Mediator in a neutral forum to reach a mutually acceptable solution. The FDMS Administrator will assign a Financial Consultant and a Mediator to work with the farmer through the mediation process. Confidentiality is extremely important to the quality and effectiveness of the service. Information obtained from the farmer and their creditor(s) is used for the sole purpose of mediation and is shared only among the parties involved in the mediation process. The shelter will be installed within Hangar 10, which has existing temperature-control capabilities, and will remain in service until the construction of the new CMMA hangar. The Composite Repair Shelter will support aircraft composite repair activities, including the application and curing of adhesives, bonds, lacquers, and resins used on composite materials such as carbon fibre, fiberglass, and aramid fibre. Limited quantities of solvents, including acetone, methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK), and methyl propyl ketone (MPK), will be used during repair operations.

tenders.description_excerpt: NRC Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics (HAA) requires extended measurement capabilities in the millimetre-wave frequency range to support ongoing research in characterizing front-end components for low-noise receivers in radio astronomy. Existing Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) at NRC HAA are currently limited to a maximum operational frequency of 116 GHz. To increase its measurement capability, NRC HAA intends to acquire frequency extender modules covering the 110–170 GHz band. These extenders must integrate with either of HAA's existing analysers (Keysight PNA N5227B and Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67), providing high dynamic range and stable two-port measurements.

The RFI seeks information on: • Current accessibility capabilities, policies, and practices relating to software, hardware, and AI systems; • Conformance with relevant accessibility standards and specifications for software, hardware, and AI systems; • Approaches to incorporating accessibility throughout the product lifecycle, including design, development, testing, deployment, and procurement; • Barriers, implementation challenges, and considerations associated with achieving accessibility; and, • Organizational readiness to meet potential future accessibility requirements. tenders.description_excerpt: Amended Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids. Novel psychoactive substances (NPS) in the illegal drug supply pose risks to Canadians. However, little is known about their pharmacological activity. More potent drugs increase the risk of overdose risks. Evidence on the pharmacological activity of these substances is essential to support scientific regulatory activities and risk assessments. The illegal drug supply is continuously evolving, with new substances continually being detected. There is a need for further information on their harms to Canadians. This procurement activity will allow for the evaluation of the in vitro pharmacological activity of two categories of emerging drugs: synthetic cannabinoids, and stimulants. The data generated from this contract will inform future assessment activities and allow the OLRA to make more informed regulatory science decisions. For both streams, they require the pharmacological testing of different classes of substances, and require acquisition of reference standards and control samples, getting licenses for controlled substances, conducting experiments (including doing statistical analysis), and finally drafting and finalizing reports. tenders.description_excerpt: The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requires the removal and replacement of two transformers at Beaver Creek Institution (Minimum) prior to December 31, 2026 to comply with federal regulations established under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act and the polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) Regulations. One existing pad-mounted transformer, installed in 1975, contains polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) at a concentration of 172 ppm, which exceeds the regulatory threshold. A second pole-mounted transformer has reached the end of its service life and, due to its age, may contain PCBs. Both transformers must be removed and replaced prior to the regulatory deadline of December 31, 2026. The work includes the supply and installation of replacement transformers, disposal of PCB-contaminated equipment and associated oil in accordance with applicable regulations, coordination of electrical outages and commissioning activities, and restoration of affected areas.

DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT This Small Craft Harbours project involves the fabrication, transportation, and delivery of twenty-three (23) floating wharf modules, each measuring 12 meters in length. The modules include Type A and Type B configurations and will be delivered on land to two public wharf locations in New Brunswick. In general, the work includes, but is not limited to, the following: 1. Cap-de-St-Louis, New Brunswick: Delivery of thirteen (13) floating wharf modules, consisting of twelve (12) Type A modules and one (1) Type B module. 2. There is limited on-site staging or laydown areas, and an off-site staging area will be required for material, equipment and helicopter long line staging. Construction activities, materials, and equipment must be transported to and from the site using helicopter-supported access, requiring careful planning and coordination to safely and efficiently execute the work within a sensitive national park environment. The requirement supports domestic operations conducted by the Canadian Army, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance activities, situational awareness, force protection, disaster response, search and rescue support, infrastructure assessment, training, and experimentation.
